For Branch 2's supporting 29-feature model, let a graph vertex \(u=(i,j)\) pair ligand feature \(i\) with receptor feature \(j\). Its allowance \(\epsilon_u\) is \(s\) when both features are hydrogen-bond donor or acceptor types (each may be either type), and \(4.0\)~\AA\ otherwise. The scalar \(s\) takes the values \(3.0\) and \(3.3\)~\AA. For distinct vertices \(u=(i,j)\) and \(v=(k,l)\), let \(d_L(i,k)\) and \(d_R(j,l)\) be the distances between their ligand and receptor feature positions respectively. An edge exists precisely when \(0.6\,\text{\AA}+\epsilon_u+\epsilon_v-|d_L(i,k)-d_R(j,l)|>0\); equality is excluded. In the feature-injective variant it also requires \(i\ne k\) and \(j\ne l\). Thus \(s\) is a per-vertex allowance used twice when both vertices qualify, not the entire pairwise mismatch tolerance or a direct ligand--receptor distance cutoff. These scalar variants belong to this supporting model, not to the separate polar or v2 allowance triples. The frozen rule and retained saved-graph audit agree on the strict inequality.\rr{branch-2 retained ada/v6-domain-frozen.txt and ada/v6\_audit.py; entry 100 identifies the repaired execution}
